findings.title: SQL injection in login form (authentication bypass)
findings.evidence: Invalid login returned HTTP 401; payload returned HTTP 302 and a session cookie. Home page then says 'Logged in as unknown user' without any password.
findings.impact: Anyone can log in as any user, including the administrator, without a password.

remediation.fix: Use parameterised queries (placeholders) instead of building SQL with string formatting. Hash passwords (bcrypt/argon2) and add rate limiting on login.
remediation.reference_patch:
row = db.execute(
    "SELECT id, username, role FROM users WHERE username=? AND password=?",
    (username, password)).fetchone()

findings.title: SQL injection
findings.evidence: Boolean proof: TRUE condition returned 349 bytes (twice, stable), FALSE condition returned 262 bytes. The database executed our logic. Rows exposed by TRUE payload: ['admin: balance hidden', 'sara: balance hidden', 'omar: balance hidden']
findings.impact: Attacker can read data they should not see (e.g. hidden products, other tables).

remediation.fix: Use parameterised queries; never concatenate user input into SQL. Apply least-privilege DB accounts.
remediation.reference_patch:
rows = db.execute(
    "SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE hidden=0 AND name LIKE ?",
    (f"%{q}%",)).fetchall()

findings.title: Missing HTTP security headers
findings.evidence: Response of GET / is missing: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.impact: No defence-in-depth against XSS, clickjacking and MIME sniffing.

remediation.fix: Add Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy.

findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting (XSS)
findings.evidence: Canary tag <cart-canary-3bd02981> came back UNESCAPED inside the HTML response, so the browser would parse attacker-controlled markup.
findings.impact: Attacker-supplied HTML/JS runs in the victim's browser (session theft, phishing).

remediation.fix: HTML-escape all user input on output (html.escape / template auto-escaping) and add a Content-Security-Policy header.
remediation.reference_patch: shown = html.escape(q)

findings.title: Sensitive information disclosure (debug endpoint)
findings.evidence: Response leaks SECRET_KEY = files-************ (redacted in report).
findings.impact: Secret key leaked: attacker can forge session cookies and impersonate any user.

remediation.fix: Remove debug endpoints in production, rotate the leaked secret, load secrets from env vars.

findings.title: Path traversal (arbitrary file read)
findings.evidence: Read the planted canary file outside the download folder: 'CART-CANARY-7cb4f4ccdcd7ef72'.
findings.impact: Attacker can read files outside the intended folder (configs, keys, source code).

remediation.fix: Resolve the final path and verify it stays inside the allowed base directory; prefer a whitelist of file names. Do NOT just strip '../' (bypassable with '....//').

findings.title: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
findings.evidence: Logged in as low-privilege 'lina' (id=2) and read 3 other accounts: id=1: username=admin, email=adm************; id=3: username=kareem, email=kar************; id=4: username=noor, email=noo************
findings.impact: A normal user can read other users' personal data (email, phone) by changing the id.

remediation.fix: Check on the server that the logged-in user owns the requested object (or is admin).
remediation.reference_patch:
if current_user.id != uid and current_user.role != 'admin':
    return jsonify(error='forbidden'), 403

findings.title: Open redirect
findings.evidence: Server answered HTTP 302 with Location: https://cart-canary.invalid/proof (redirect NOT followed - policy).
findings.impact: Trusted domain can be abused to send victims to phishing sites.

remediation.fix: Only allow relative paths (starting with a single '/') or a whitelist of domains.
remediation.reference_patch:
if not (nxt.startswith('/') and not nxt.startswith('//')):
    nxt = '/'

findings.title: Privilege escalation to administrator (chained attack)
findings.evidence: Chain F06 -> /admin: normal user gets HTTP 403, but the session obtained through SQL injection (as 'admin.') gets HTTP 200 on the protected page.
findings.impact: Full admin control: list of all users and their emails exposed.

remediation.fix: Fix the root cause (login SQL injection). Add MFA for admin accounts and log admin logins.
